evidence_items.publisher: Proof News and the Institute for Advanced Study, AI Democracy Projects

receipt.public_excerpt: Team majorities rated half of the 130 responses as inaccurate.

evidence_items.explanation: Experts evaluated 26 ordinary election questions across five leading models; errors included incorrect contact details and fabricated information. GPT-4 performed substantially better, with 19% of its responses rated inaccurate, and the authors explicitly warn that this small, nonrandom sample is not representative of everyday usage.

evidence_items.locator: Core questions about mistake identification, question 1
evidence_items.explanation: The researchers found difficulty locating simple, unambiguous reasoning mistakes, but the underlying study was already public in 2023. Its deliberately error-enriched dataset also cannot estimate the frequency of mistakes in ordinary model use.

unresolved_gaps: There is no representative error rate covering all deep-learning systems and ordinary user interactions.
The decisive evaluation covers factual election questions, not the full range of elementary reasoning tasks.
